title: Edmund and the Inheritance
premise: True-crime podcaster Ivo Galloway has spent two years dissecting the 1974 disappearance of heiress Edmund Vane, a case closed as an accident. When a letter arrives confessing to Edmund's murder—postmarked the day after the last surviving witness's funeral—Ivo realizes the killer is still alive, still watching, and feeding her clues like a game. As she digs, she discovers the confession writer knows details never made public, and that her own late mother was the detective who buried the truth. The killer turns out to be Edmund's presumed-dead brother, living under a stolen identity, who killed to claim the inheritance and has spent fifty years eliminating anyone who remembered. In the climax, Ivo lures him into confessing on-air at the abandoned Vane estate, where he nearly kills her before police—tipped by her producer—intervene; the final chapters reveal her mother's cover-up was protection, not corruption, and Ivo must choose between exposing it all or honoring the love that motivated it.
about_author: Ivo Brightwater is the pen name of a former court reporter who spent a decade transcribing other people's worst days before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town full of unsolved histories and writes mysteries about the stories families tell to survive themselves.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Ivo Galloway records the finale of her podcast on the Vane case when a cream envelope arrives: a full confession to Edmund Vane's murder, postmarked the day after witness Arthur Pell's funeral. Her POV establishes obsession and unease. Emotional beat: the thrill of being chosen curdling into fear—someone wanted her to have this.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Ivo reconstructs the 1974 case: Edmund Vane, 24, vanished from the family estate; ruled accidental drowning; body never found. Through archival research and an interview with retired journalist Marge Okafor, we learn three witnesses are now dead within eighteen months. Beat: dread—the pattern only visible from above.

chapters.title: What Arthur Knew
chapters.summary: Ivo attends the tail end of Arthur Pell's estate sale and finds his annotated copy of the case file, with one margin note: 'She wasn't alone on the water.' A stranger watches her from across the yard. Beat: first contact with the hunter; paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: Mother's Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV shifts inward: her mother, Detective Ruth Galloway, worked the original case and died refusing to discuss it. Searching Ruth's things, Ivo finds a key and a photo of Ruth with the Vane family—far too friendly for a mere investigator. Beat: personal betrayal begins to shadow the professional mystery.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Another letter arrives, containing a detail never released: the color of Edmund's rowboat cushion. Police dismiss Ivo; Detective Sergeant Nnamdi Cole warns her she's being groomed. Beat: validation and isolation—she believes him, no one else does.

chapters.title: Vane House, Empty
chapters.summary: Ivo breaks into the derelict Vane estate and finds the boathouse restored—newly varnished wood in a house dead for decades. Someone maintains it. She hears footsteps and flees. Beat: terror made physical; the past is not past, it's kept.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Drowned
chapters.summary: Research chapter: Edmund's younger brother Casper reportedly died abroad in 1971—yet Ivo finds a 1976 photograph of a man with his face, alive, at the funeral of the family solicitor. Beat: the puzzle clicks into a darker shape; identity itself becomes suspect.

chapters.title: Marge Remembers
chapters.summary: POV alternates with elderly journalist Marge Okafor, who recalls young Casper Vane as gentle, eclipsed by his brilliant sister—and recalls Ruth Galloway quietly warning sources to forget things. Beat: sympathy complicates suspicion; even the villain may be a victim of something.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: The podcast's hosting platform pulls episodes after legal threats from a foundation bearing the Vane name. Ivo's producer, Dev, urges her to stop; they fight. That night her apartment is searched, nothing taken but her mother's key. Beat: the cost escalates; love and duty pull Dev and Ivo apart.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: A letter addressed to 'Ruth's girl' reveals the writer knew her mother personally—and claims Ruth protected him. Ivo, furious and grieving, confronts the possibility her mother shielded a murderer. Beat: the theme sharpens—love against duty, inherited sin.

chapters.title: Following the Money
chapters.summary: Forensic accountant friend traces the Vane inheritance: a trust that pays out annually to a beneficiary named 'E. Marsh,' active since 1975. The payments route through a shell company tied to a respected local philanthropist. Beat: rising tension—the killer has been hiding in plain sight, honored by the community.

chapters.title: Tea with Mr. Marsh
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews Edwin Marsh, charming benefactor and pillar of the town, and recognizes Casper Vane's eyes. He knows exactly who she is and speaks in double meanings about sisters, debt, and what families owe. Beat: cat-and-mouse begins openly; he is delighted to be nearly caught.

chapters.title: What Edmund Found
chapters.summary: Through Marge and a hidden diary fragment, the backstory emerges: Edmund discovered Casper had been embezzling from the trust to fund a new life; she threatened to expose him the day she vanished. Beat: motive revealed—but also doubt. Was Edmund crueler than the record shows?

chapters.title: Ruth's Tape
chapters.summary: The stolen key fits a safe-deposit box holding a cassette: Ruth's recorded interview with a terrified young man the night after Edmund disappeared—a confession she chose to bury. Ivo hears her mother choose love and duty over law. Beat: devastating midpoint reversal; the hero's moral ground cracks.

chapters.title: Dev's Discovery
chapters.summary: Producer Dev, working separately, matches the letters' typewriter ribbon to a machine donated to the town historical society—a place Edwin Marsh chairs. He tells Ivo they can go to Cole now. She hesitates: exposing Marsh means exposing Ruth. Beat: conflict between partners; duty versus blood, again.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Baited
chapters.summary: Ivo proposes the dangerous plan: announce a final live episode revealing 'the killer's identity' without naming him, forcing Marsh to come silence her publicly. Cole agrees to surveillance; Dev hates every second of it. Beat: resolve hardening into recklessness; love expressed as fear.

chapters.title: Nineteen Seventy-Four, Retold
chapters.summary: The live episode airs: Ivo narrates the true story of Edmund's death—Casper struck her during an argument at the boathouse, then staged the drowning while Ruth arrived too late to stop the cover-up he begged for. Listenership explodes. Beat: catharsis and exposure; the trap springs.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Marsh comes to Vane House during the broadcast, expecting to find Ivo alone. Instead she confronts him with the tape playing. He disarms her, confesses with terrible tenderness—he has kept the boathouse beautiful for fifty years out of guilt and love. Beat: climax; the killer is human, which makes him worse.

chapters.title: Cole's Hour
chapters.summary: Detective Cole and officers arrive seconds after Marsh forces Ivo toward the water—the same water. His arrest is quiet, almost relieved. Ivo, shaking, realizes she reenacted her mother's worst night and survived where Ruth couldn't act. Beat: release of tension; survival and its aftershock.

chapters.title: What Ruth Chose
chapters.summary: Fallout: the tape makes Ruth's obstruction public. Ivo must decide whether to air it. Learning Ruth buried the confession to protect a dying Arthur Pell's family from reprisal—not to protect Casper—she chooses context over cruelty. Beat: resolution of the identity theme; forgiving the mother, keeping the truth.

chapters.title: Edmund, At Last
chapters.summary: Edmund's remains are recovered from the old well beneath the boathouse floor and laid to rest. The town reckons with its honored citizen's crimes; the trust is dissolved into a scholarship in Edmund's name. Beat: mourning, restitution, quiet justice.

chapters.title: The Last Episode
chapters.summary: Months later, Ivo records the series finale with Dev beside her—partners again, maybe more. She reads a final letter, this one from Edmund's own hand, found in the well wall: a message to whoever loved her enough to look. Ivo signs off, free of the case but changed by it. Beat: peace earned; love and duty finally aligned.
